children: Gold prices fall in early European trading, but hold above $4,500 a troy ounce as investors await the release of key U.S. payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next move. New York futures are down 0.6% to $4,513.90 a troy ounce, on track for a modest weekly loss. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said Thursday he would support holding rates steady if August inflation data continue the recent progress seen in June and July. According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders are now pricing in a 50% possibility that the Fed will raise interest rates this month. "Going forward, U.S. payrolls and next week's inflation data will be critical for the Fed outlook, with further evidence of disinflation likely to support gold," says Soojin Kim from MUFG. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
